title: Weather vs Climate + Season vs Temperature

voice.name: Liam (ElevenLabs default — young, energetic American; works on the free plan)

pauseRule: "pause" = TOTAL silence (seconds) after that line — only on important beats (hook question, topic switch, into recap, before CTA).
artNote: Hook = surprising-fact intro scene (950x630) that teases pair 2's payoff: a smiling sun with spinning rays, an orange 'closest!' arrow to a tilted Earth (north leaning away), a swinging JAN calendar, a shivering snowman in falling snow, ? marks. p1 cards: weather = clock hand spinning, rain falling, sun peeking from a cloud; climate = 30-year chart, spiky blue daily line + orange average line that draws in, a dot riding it. p2 cards: season = four-season wheel (flower/sun/leaf/snowflake) with a turning hand + tilted Earth 23.4°; temperature = thermometer whose red level rises and falls, hot sun vs cold snowflake. Joe's tip tile = new tall tile with its own scene: grumpy wobbling rain cloud with a jittering lightning bolt (WEATHER) vs a calm sun in sunglasses with spinning rays (CLIMATE).

lines.text: Earth is closest to the sun in January. So why is it cold?
Weather is right now. It changes by the hour.
Climate is the average weather over 30 years.
In 2018, it snowed in the Sahara. That's weather.
A season is a time of year, caused by Earth's tilt.
Temperature is how hot or cold it is.
In January, Earth is 5 million kilometers closer to the sun.
But the north tilts away. Temperatures drop.
My trick: weather is your mood. Climate is your personality.
